about: Machine-readable inventory of every tunable setting. Checked against the code by tests/test_settings_manifest.py and rendered by scripts/gen_settings_doc.py into docs/wiki/Settings-Reference.md. Examples use documentation ranges only. Secrets list names, never values.

stacks/00-foundation.name: region
stacks/00-foundation.description: DigitalOcean region slug. Names are built from resource_key, which defaults to this. Check the sizes your account may use in the region (GET /v2/sizes) before changing it.
stacks/00-foundation.validation: ^[a-z]{3}[0-9]$ (three lowercase letters and a digit); the pattern cannot know which sizes the account may use
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/00-foundation.name: vpc_ip_range
stacks/00-foundation.description: Private CIDR for the VPC. Must be the network address and must not overlap any range in reserved_ranges.
stacks/00-foundation.validation: private IPv4 CIDR (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, also checked in modules/vpc); the network address (10.78.0.0/24, not 10.78.0.5/24); prefix length between /16 and /28; no overlap with reserved_ranges (a precondition on the project, because OpenTofu 1.8 cannot compare two variables in a validation)
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)
stacks/00-foundation.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/00-foundation.name: project_name
stacks/00-foundation.description: Name of the DigitalOcean project that groups the resources (the code has no description for it).
stacks/00-foundation.validation: none today (DigitalOcean's allowed character set is UNVERIFIED)
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/00-foundation.name: reserved_ranges
stacks/00-foundation.description: Private CIDRs the VPC range must not overlap (your homelab, other VPCs). Optional; they identify your network, so they are never committed. Prompts the human check, does not replace it.
stacks/00-foundation.validation: each entry an IPv4 CIDR; vpc_ip_range must not overlap any entry (compared by first and last address)
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_reserved_ranges, a JSON list) or a private tfvars today; Doppler only once a hook line in .spacelift/config.yml requests it (the foundation hooks request only DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN)
stacks/00-foundation.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/00-foundation.name: resource_key
stacks/00-foundation.description: Key used in the names and tags of cloud and Twingate objects instead of region; empty means region, so every name is identical to a stack that never set it. IMMUTABLE for the life of a stack: changing it changes names, causes widespread plan changes and may replace resources, including through tags or user_data. Never derived from site_name.
stacks/00-foundation.validation: empty, or ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,23}$; immutable on a live stack
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/00-foundation.name: site_name
stacks/00-foundation.description: Telemetry label for the site (metrics and log labels in a later stage); empty means site-<region>. In no resource name, tag or output; changing it replaces nothing.
stacks/00-foundation.validation: empty, or ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,23}$; unique across sites (a rule for the person, one stack cannot test it)
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/00-foundation.name: provider_name
stacks/00-foundation.description: Label for the cloud provider; does not select modules.
stacks/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: host_firewall
stacks/10-access.description: A default-drop host firewall (nftables table inet cah_host, input chain only) on each connector, a second layer behind the cloud firewall. Only loopback, established traffic, the ICMP and DHCP the network card needs, TCP 22 from host_firewall_ssh_sources and, when connector_telemetry.metrics_port is set, that port from the same sources are let in. Default false is the live state: merging code with this unset plans no change. true adds a script, a systemd unit and the nftables package through user_data, which REPLACES the droplet of every connector in host_firewall_instances (both by default). The script checks the ruleset, applies it, verifies sshd still listens and removes the table if not. Roll out one connector at a time: true with host_firewall_instances ["a"], apply, check SSH through Twingate, then ["a", "b"]. Not yet tested on a real machine.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: host_firewall_instances
stacks/10-access.description: Which connectors get host_firewall: a, b or both. Only matters once host_firewall is true. Set ["a"] first, apply, check SSH through Twingate to the new connector, then ["a", "b"]. A connector not listed runs without the host firewall, as it does today.
stacks/10-access.validation: at least one entry; each entry is a or b, no repeats
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: host_firewall_ssh_sources
stacks/10-access.description: IPv4 CIDRs allowed to reach TCP 22 (and the connector metrics port) through the host firewall. Default the three private RFC 1918 blocks: the cloud firewall already limits SSH to the connector tag and this only narrows it to private space, because the module does not know the VPC CIDR. Narrow it to your VPC range if you know it. Only matters once host_firewall is true.
stacks/10-access.validation: at least one IPv4 CIDR, no repeats (host bits and IPv6 are refused)
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: region
stacks/10-access.description: DigitalOcean region slug, from the foundation stack's region output. Names are built from resource_key, which defaults to this.
stacks/10-access.set_where: Spacelift stack dependency, mapped to a TF_VAR_* environment variable (output of stack 00)

stacks/10-access.name: vpc_id
stacks/10-access.description: ID of the VPC created by stack 00 (the code has no description for it).
stacks/10-access.set_where: Spacelift stack dependency, mapped to a TF_VAR_* environment variable (output of stack 00)

stacks/10-access.name: project_id
stacks/10-access.description: ID of the DigitalOcean project created by stack 00 (the code has no description for it).
stacks/10-access.set_where: Spacelift stack dependency, mapped to a TF_VAR_* environment variable (output of stack 00)

stacks/10-access.name: baseline_tag
stacks/10-access.description: Baseline firewall tag created by stack 00; the connectors carry it.
stacks/10-access.set_where: Spacelift stack dependency, mapped to a TF_VAR_* environment variable (output of stack 00)

stacks/10-access.name: twingate_network
stacks/10-access.description: Bare Twingate network subdomain (the tenant name).
stacks/10-access.set_where: Doppler (config prd), exported as TF_VAR_* by the Spacelift hook (TWINGATE_NETWORK)
stacks/10-access.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/10-access.name: admin_ssh_public_key
stacks/10-access.description: Public SSH key for the cah-admin user on the connectors: '<algorithm> <key>' with an optional trailing comment of one word. The comment is dropped before cloud-init, so user_data does not depend on it.
stacks/10-access.validation: ^(ssh-ed25519|ssh-rsa|ecdsa-sha2-nistp(256|384|521)) [A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*( [A-Za-z0-9@._+:=/-]{1,64})?$ (one optional comment word of safe characters; no line break or other whitespace); the same check in modules/twingate-bootstrap
stacks/10-access.set_where: Doppler (config prd), exported as TF_VAR_* by the Spacelift hook (ADMIN_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY)
stacks/10-access.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/10-access.name: admin_ssh_key_name
stacks/10-access.description: Name of an SSH key already registered on the DigitalOcean account.
stacks/10-access.set_where: Doppler (config prd), exported as TF_VAR_* by the Spacelift hook (ADMIN_SSH_KEY_NAME)
stacks/10-access.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/10-access.name: admin_user_ids
stacks/10-access.description: Twingate user ids placed in the admin group.
stacks/10-access.set_where: Doppler (config prd), exported as TF_VAR_* by the Spacelift hook (ADMIN_USER_IDS, a JSON list)
stacks/10-access.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

stacks/10-access.name: resource_key
stacks/10-access.description: Key used in the names and tags of cloud and Twingate objects instead of region; empty means region, so every name is identical to a stack that never set it. IMMUTABLE for the life of a stack: changing it changes names, causes widespread plan changes and may replace resources, including through tags or user_data. Never derived from site_name.
stacks/10-access.validation: empty, or ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,23}$; immutable on a live stack
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: site_name
stacks/10-access.description: Telemetry label for the site (metrics and log labels in a later stage); empty means site-<region>. In no resource name, tag or output; changing it replaces nothing.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: provider_name
stacks/10-access.description: Label for the cloud provider; does not select modules.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: reboot_times
stacks/10-access.description: Reboot time per connector (HH:MM, America/New_York, the droplet's local time). Keys a and b. The defaults are the times the live connectors use.
stacks/10-access.validation: exactly the keys a and b; each HH:MM in 24-hour time; the two reboot times at least 60 minutes apart, measured around the clock across midnight, which also keeps each connector's weekly update (reboot + 30 minutes) at least 30 minutes from the other's reboot
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: timezone
stacks/10-access.description: IANA time zone of the machines, also the zone reboot_time(s) and the weekly connector update are read in. Replaces a literal in the cloud-init template; the default renders byte-identical user_data.
stacks/10-access.validation: ^(UTC|[A-Za-z_]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+){1,2})$ (an IANA-shaped name; line breaks, spaces and YAML-special characters are rejected) and the name must be listed in modules/twingate-bootstrap/timezones.txt (generated by scripts/gen_timezones.py; enforced in the bootstrap module, which every stack goes through). Changing it changes user_data, which is force-new and replaces the droplets
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: connector_telemetry_previous
stacks/10-access.type: object({status_updates_enabled = optional(bool), log_level = optional(number), connection_logs = optional(bool, false), metrics_port = optional(number), labels = optional(map(string), {})})
stacks/10-access.description: What the connectors NOT listed in connector_telemetry_instances keep: the telemetry they run today. Default {} is right for the first activation. For a later change (say log_level 5 to 7) set connector_telemetry to the new value, this to the old value and connector_telemetry_instances to ["a"]; apply, check SSH through Twingate, then set instances to ["a", "b"] and clear this. Without it connector b would lose its telemetry and be replaced in the same plan as a.
stacks/10-access.validation: none (the bootstrap module validates it, the same checks as connector_telemetry); non-nullable (null means {})
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: connector_telemetry_instances
stacks/10-access.description: Which connectors get connector_telemetry: a, b or both. Only matters once connector_telemetry is set. Set ["a"] first, apply, check SSH through Twingate to the new connector, then ["a", "b"]: that is the one-at-a-time rollout. A connector not listed gets the default (nothing).
stacks/10-access.validation: at least one entry; each entry is a or b, no repeats
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: connector_telemetry
stacks/10-access.type: object({status_updates_enabled = optional(bool), log_level = optional(number), connection_logs = optional(bool, false), metrics_port = optional(number), labels = optional(map(string), {})})
stacks/10-access.description: Twingate connector telemetry for both connectors. Default {} is the live state and changes nothing. status_updates_enabled is a provider setting that is not sent while unset, and replaces nothing. log_level (TWINGATE_LOG_LEVEL), connection_logs (true writes TWINGATE_LOG_ANALYTICS=v3), metrics_port (TWINGATE_METRICS_PORT) and labels (TWINGATE_LABEL_<KEY>) add lines to /etc/twingate/connector.conf: that changes user_data and the plan shows the droplets of every connector in connector_telemetry_instances REPLACED (both by default). Roll out one connector at a time with connector_telemetry_instances, with an SSH-through-Twingate check between (Trace-One-Change-End-to-End, variant C). Opens no firewall port. Labels are shown in the Twingate Admin Console: never put a secret in one.
stacks/10-access.validation: log_level in {3, 4, 5, 7} or unset; metrics_port a whole number 1024 to 65535 and not 9100, or unset; labels: at most 10, keys ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,31}$, values ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ (no spaces, quotes or line breaks, because they are written into the connector config); connector_telemetry is non-nullable (null means {})
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_connector_telemetry as JSON)
stacks/10-access.example: { log_level = 5, connection_logs = true, metrics_port = 9999, labels = { DEPLOYED_BY = "opentofu" } }

stacks/10-access.name: metadata_lock
stacks/10-access.description: Lock the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254, which serves each connector's user-data and so its Twingate tokens) to root and to the do-agent user (DigitalOcean's monitoring agent reads it; allowed only when that user exists). Default false is the live state: merging code with this unset plans no change. true adds an nftables table, a script and a systemd unit through user_data, which REPLACES the droplet of every connector in metadata_lock_instances (both by default). Roll out one connector at a time: true with metadata_lock_instances ["a"], apply, check SSH through Twingate, then ["a", "b"]. Not yet tested on a real machine.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: metadata_lock_instances
stacks/10-access.description: Which connectors get metadata_lock: a, b or both. Only matters once metadata_lock is true. Set ["a"] first, apply, check SSH through Twingate to the new connector, then ["a", "b"]. A connector not listed runs without the lock, as it does today.
stacks/10-access.validation: at least one entry; each entry is a or b, no repeats
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: metrics_enabled
stacks/10-access.description: Install node exporter and expose connector metrics.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: node_exporter_port
stacks/10-access.description: Node exporter port.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: metrics_port_connector
stacks/10-access.description: Connector metrics port.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: wazuh_agent_group
stacks/10-access.description: Wazuh agent group for the cloud hosts.
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/10-access.name: labels
stacks/10-access.description: Telemetry labels.
stacks/10-access.validation: keys limited to env, role, owner_team; values at most 32 characters
stacks/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/aws/00-foundation.name: region
stacks/aws/00-foundation.description: AWS region name. The price table was recorded for us-east-1; another region needs its own check.
stacks/aws/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/aws/00-foundation.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/aws/10-access.description: Lock the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254, which serves each connector's user-data and so its Twingate tokens) to root and to the do-agent user (DigitalOcean's monitoring agent reads it; allowed only when that user exists). Default false is the live state: merging code with this unset plans no change. true adds an nftables table, a script and a systemd unit through user_data, which REPLACES the instance of every connector in metadata_lock_instances (both by default). Roll out one connector at a time: true with metadata_lock_instances ["a"], apply, check SSH through Twingate, then ["a", "b"]. Not yet tested on a real machine.
stacks/aws/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/aws/10-access.name: metadata_lock_instances
stacks/aws/10-access.description: Which connectors get metadata_lock: a, b or both. Only matters once metadata_lock is true. Set ["a"] first, apply, check SSH through Twingate to the new connector, then ["a", "b"]. A connector not listed runs without the lock, as it does today.
stacks/aws/10-access.validation: at least one entry; each entry is a or b, no repeats
stacks/aws/10-access.set_where: tfvars (local plans) or Spacelift stack environment (TF_VAR_*)

stacks/20-telemetry.name: metrics_enabled

stacks/20-telemetry.readers: UNVERIFIED: Doppler config members and Spacelift stack environment readers; filled in during step 2

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: security_group_id
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: The one security group attached to the instance's network interface at launch, so there is no unprotected moment. From the firewall module's id (its single rule target). A single string, not a list: security group rules are additive, so any second group a caller added could open inbound access to the public address.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: see the validation block in variables.tf
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: instance_type
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: EC2 instance type. The stack reads it from cost.json (local.<x>.type) so the price and the plan can never disagree.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: see the validation block in variables.tf
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: architecture
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: CPU architecture of the Ubuntu image: arm64 (Graviton types such as t4g) or amd64 (types such as t3). Must match instance_type.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: see the validation block in variables.tf
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: root_volume_size
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Root disk size in GiB (gp3). This number is an input to the cost gate: the AMI's own default is not priced, so the size is always set here. 8 GiB is the smallest the Ubuntu image accepts.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: see the validation block in variables.tf
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: remote_network_id
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Twingate remote network (site) shared by every connector of the stack.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: instance
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: One lowercase letter or digit that tells this connector from its siblings (a, b).
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: none in this module (the bootstrap module checks it)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: twingate_network
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Bare Twingate network subdomain (acme for acme.twingate.com). Sensitive because the tenant slug identifies the tenant.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: none in this module (the bootstrap module checks it)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.readers: same as the calling stack's variable of the same name

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: admin_ssh_public_key
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Public key (type and key, no comment) for the cah-admin user. Installed by cloud-init; no AWS key pair is used.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: none in this module (the bootstrap module checks it)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.readers: same as the calling stack's variable of the same name

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: reboot_time
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: HH:MM (in timezone, the instance's local time) when unattended-upgrades may reboot this instance. Give each connector a different time so they never reboot together.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: none in this module (the bootstrap module checks it)
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: timezone
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: IANA time zone of the machines, also the zone reboot_time(s) and the weekly connector update are read in. Replaces a literal in the cloud-init template; the default renders byte-identical user_data.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: ^(UTC|[A-Za-z_]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+){1,2})$ (an IANA-shaped name; line breaks, spaces and YAML-special characters are rejected) and the name must be listed in modules/twingate-bootstrap/timezones.txt (generated by scripts/gen_timezones.py; enforced in the bootstrap module, which every stack goes through). Changing it changes user_data, which is force-new and replaces the droplets
modules/aws/twingate-connector.set_where: set by the calling stack (not a user setting)

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: connector_telemetry
modules/aws/twingate-connector.type: object({status_updates_enabled = optional(bool), log_level = optional(number), connection_logs = optional(bool, false), metrics_port = optional(number), labels = optional(map(string), {})})
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Connector telemetry, passed to the bootstrap module (which validates it). Default {} changes nothing. log_level, connection_logs, metrics_port and labels change user_data and replace the instance; status_updates_enabled does not. Labels are shown in the Twingate Admin Console: never put a secret in one.
modules/aws/twingate-connector.validation: none (validated in modules/twingate-bootstrap); connector_telemetry is non-nullable (null means {})
modules/aws/twingate-connector.example: { log_level = 5, connection_logs = true, metrics_port = 9999, labels = { DEPLOYED_BY = "opentofu" } }

modules/aws/twingate-connector.name: metadata_lock
modules/aws/twingate-connector.description: Lock the metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) to root and the do-agent user. Default false changes nothing: user_data is byte-identical (golden hashes in the tests). true adds an nftables table, a script, a systemd unit and the nftables package to user_data, which replaces the instance.

manifests.name: connector-a size
manifests.validation: price must exist in docs/cost-prices.json; both connectors are kept equal by a test

manifests.name: connector-a backups
manifests.validation: false or true; true adds 20% of the droplet price

manifests.name: stage 0 resources
manifests.validation: list of costed resources; empty because stage 0 costs nothing

manifests.name: approved monthly total (DigitalOcean)
manifests.validation: the computed total may not exceed it; the sum across providers may not exceed the ceiling

manifests.name: monthly ceiling (current phase)
manifests.validation: dollars; one ceiling per phase in phases, the one named by current_phase is enforced; a later phase may raise it, lowering needs lowers: true, and hard_max (required, with hard_max_reason) caps every phase

manifests.name: droplet price table entry
manifests.validation: dollars per month for a size; a size absent from the table fails the gate

manifests.name: AWS connector-a instance type
manifests.validation: price must exist in docs/cost-prices/aws.json; read by the stack as local.connector_a.type; both connectors are kept equal by a test

manifests.name: AWS connector-b instance type
manifests.validation: price must exist in docs/cost-prices/aws.json; read by the stack as local.connector_b.type; both connectors are kept equal by a test

manifests.name: approved monthly total (AWS)
manifests.validation: the computed AWS total may not exceed it; counted against the ceiling only while the AWS entry is active
